In 2019, Danny Boyle, who was originally named the director for the James Bond film that eventually became No Time to Die, suggested Robert Pattinson as the man to take over as the next person to play Bond. Now, seven years later, that prediction has come true, as Pattinson was officially named the next 007 last week. Boyle isn’t done making suggestions, however, but now he’s switched to who should play the villain: Jack O’Connell.

In an interview on Alchemy with Anthony Mason, while promoting his new movie Ink, Mason brought up Boyle’s prognostication, and Boyle took it one step further, saying:

But we have an actor in [Ink], Jack O'Connell, [who] would have been a great Bond, as well.  And now I can see that in all this talk, they're talking about Jack O'Connell as a possible villain. They have that thing you want to watch them.  And it's impossible to quantify what it is. Otherwise, we’d all buy it for ourselves.

O’Connell was one of the (many) actors who were rumored to be in the running for Bond 26 before Amazon MGM and director Denis Villeneuve ultimately decided to go with Pattinson, and I think his take on O’Connell as the villain is also an inspired idea as well. Along with who could be the next “Bond Girl,” the next Bond Villain is another big casting chip that still needs to fall soon before filming kicks off, hopefully in 2027.

O’Connell isn’t the only name being bandied about to play James Bond’s next villain. Another actor who has worked with Boyle before, Cillian Murphy, has been a popular choice among fans. Barry Keoghan, who worked with Murphy on the 2026 movie schedule in Peaky Blinders: The Immortal Man (which was headed up by Bond 26 writer Steven Knight), is also a top pick. Idris Elba, whom many hoped (including me) could be the next Bond, though even he admitted he’s too old for the role now, is also a common name thrown out there (and honestly, maybe my pick).

Last week, after the Pattinson announcement, Brad Pitt even tossed his own name into the ring for the role. Now that would be an interesting choice! The latest rumors also point to Tom Hardy as the next villain, which would set up an interesting dynamic between the current Batman (Pattinson) and a former Batman villain (Hardy played Bane in The Dark Knight Rises).

There are still quite a few casting announcements for Bond 26 to look forward to, like M, Q, and Moneypenny, in addition to the villain, maybe a henchman or two, and, of course, the next Bond Girl. Oh, and who could possibly be in line to do the next Bond theme? It’s an exciting time to be a Bond fan. Meanwhile, Ink will be available to watch with a Netflix subscription on January 8th, after a short stint in theaters starting on December 11.

#3561. Diablo 4 Is Making Helltides A Hell Of A Lot Easier

One of Diablo 4's oldest endgame activities, Helltides, is getting a major refresh for Season 16.

As detailed by developer Blizzard in their full breakdown of Season of Tyrael's Gambit, Helltides will soon be far more efficient to run than before. The whole point of the activity is to kill as many demons as fast as possible, acquire the Aberrant Cinders they drop, and then use those cinders to open chests for items.

Dying means losing half of the cinders you've collected, but they are also lost when the Helltide ends. Oftentimes that means having left over amounts of cinders you can't spend, only to then go to the next Helltide five minutes later and repeat the process from zero. It's been this way since Diablo 4 launched back in 2023.

In Season 16, that will finally change. Blizzard is getting rid of the downtime between Helltides spawning and making it so there will always be a Helltide up in one of the game's original zones, as well as one in expansion areas like Hahantu or Skovos. Even better, Aberrant Cinders won't be lost once a Helltide ends. Instead, players can collect up to 5,000 cinders at a time to be spent on opening chests within the activity. Additionally, the overall loot quality from opening chests in the Helltide will be improved and chests can be opened instantly.

Those changes should go a long way towards making Helltides feel more valuable and efficient when trying to farm gear, as you can now blast demons to your heart's content until reaching the Aberrant Cinder cap. Just don't die while you have a full 5,000 stored up. 

Diablo 4 Season 16 launches December 1. Alongside its Helltide changes, the season will bring big updates to War Plans as well. A new system, War Plans Tactics, will give players more control over what activities appear in their War Plans, as well as more options when it comes to rerolling them and the rewards they grant. Players will also have new Horadric items to chase that will modify specific Talisman sets, greatly increasing their power. 

Blizzard additionally announced many of the features that were added as part of Diablo 4 Season 15, Hell's Legacy, will be made permanent. Those additions include the season's capstone dungeons, optional bosses like Moophisto, the Annihilus Seal, Hellfire Torch Charm, and the season's legacy Unique items like Stone of Jordan.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

Yellowjackets, the time-hopping survival drama about a group of teenage girls who are stranded in the wilderness in 1996 and do terrible things to survive, is coming to an end. Whether or not it sticks the landing, it's been one helluva ride, and we'll soon have room in the streaming schedule for other other shows about young people having a pretty rough go of it while just trying to survive.

Situated between flashbacks and flash-forwards (not entirely unlike Yellowjackets), mystery/thriller The Wilds sees an airplane full of teenage girls crash on the way to an empowerment program in Hawaii. It quickly becomes clear that the accident was engineered and that the whole thing is some sort of social experiment, and the survivors are forced to compete against each other if they want to live. The show understands the ways in which young women are exploited and expected to compete against each other in the real world, not just a show about girlfights. Stream The Wilds on Prime Video.

A bit more grounded...but only at first glance, The Stranded takes place on a Thai island in the midst of a tsunami. The island was formerly home to a prestigious high school, and a bunch of students have snuck back for an ill-timed party on the last day of class. A bad idea, clearly, after the storm hits. Kraam (Papangkorn Lerkchaleampote), one of the few students who actually lives on the island, is trapped there along with a couple dozen classmates. Kraam knows the island, but Anan (Chutavuth Pattarakampol) assumes leadership while other students either take on necessary roles or fall in line. As the miniseries progresses, the new social order breaks down, even as the island's mysteries reveal themselves and things get weirder and more complex. Stream The Stranded on Netflix.

A handful of influencers get invited to a remote island, which is obviously a very good thing to agree to that will not lead to dramatic complications in any way. Behind the neon-lit party vibes, there's a cult at work and some ritualistic shenanigans with deadly consequences. Eden is more concerned with the survival horror than with some of the deeper themes and mysteries of Yellowjackets, but we're still playing with shifting power dynamics in this Spanish import. Stream Welcome to Eden on Netflix.

The premise of The Leftovers is brilliantly subdued: Around two percent of the world's population disappears without explanation, and it's enough to upend just about everything. Politics have adapted to the new normal, religions have collapsed and reformed, and families have had to make peace with the inexplicable loss of loved ones. The first season revolves around the Garvey family, led by Kevin (Justin Theroux), a sheriff whose wife (Amy Brenneman) left him to join a cult, while subsequent seasons broaden the scope to bring in other characters in other locations. It's more philosophical than Yellowjackets, and quieter, but the shows share an interest in the lingering effects of trauma, and in the stuff we get up to under threat and in the dark. Stream The Leftovers on HBO Max.

The 100 tells the story of the descendants of refugees of nuclear devastation who return to Earth from their habitat in space to encounter the remnants of humanity who have survived on Earth. Naturally, the first people sent to scope things out are the juvenile delinquents (better them than me), and they discover that three civilizations have risen up in the aftermath of the apocalypse, and they are all pretty scary (including one populated by cannibals, naturally). More sci-fi than horror, but the survivalist themes and mysteries here make it more than a decent match. The show builds an impressive mythology over the course of its run, leading to a conclusion that’s borderline metaphysical. Stream The 100 on Pluto TV or buy it from Prime Video.

When pretty, popular girl Kate Wallis (Olivia Holt) goes missing without a trace in 1993, awkward Jeanette Turner (Chiara Aurelia) steps in to fill the gap, modeling herself after Kate by working her way into the missing girl's social circle and getting close with her boyfriend. That's all going great until Kate reappears two years later, accusing Jeanette of having witnessed the events around her disappearance and keeping quiet. Whoops. There's even more going on, as the show shifts back and forth between 1993, 1994, and 1995 to slowly reveal the missing pieces. Season two takes on a different story set in 1999 and 2000, and the forthcoming (surprise) third season will shake things up again. The emphasis here is on mystery, but it's a show about the aftereffects of trauma and of the dark secrets that can tear families and communities apart. Stream Cruel Summer on Hulu.

A massive apocalyptic tidal wave strikes during the 10-year reunion of the graduating class of an all-girls high school. The event leaves them all trapped together (a nightmare in any event), and forced to survive while reliving old struggles and dramas. It's Yellowjackets-esque, absolutely, but also Australian and a comedy, which doesn't feel like as much of a stretch as you'd think given the over-the-top nature of that show. Stream Class of '07 on Prime Video.

A remote, charming town with some deep, dark secrets (the biggest of which, and one that it shares with Yellowjackets, is rather strongly hinted in the title), Gannibal stars Yuya Yagira as Daigo Agawa, a police officer from the big city who takes a job in the super cute (and, of course, remote) village of Kuge following some personal trouble. The perfectly charming Goto family runs the town, more or less, and welcomes Daigo and his family. It's all looking pretty great—until a mysterious man gives Daigo's daughter a severed finger as a gift, and his wife Yuki finds the words "Run Away" scrawled over a door in their new home. Just a couple of reasons why I'm more of a city person. Stream Gannibal on Disney+ and Hulu.

This latter-day plane crash narrative goes all-in on mystery and philosophy, virtually pioneering the timey-wimey reveal format that makes Yellowjackets so juicy. We kick off with flashbacks that peel back the layers of the various crash survivors before diving headfirst into warm-weather polar bears and mysterious underground bunkers and monsters made of smoke. Whether it's an uncommonly smart network show that rewards careful viewing or a load of nonsense is in the eye of the beholder—but it remains one of the most discussed and debated shows in TV history. Stream Lost on Disney+ and Hulu.

Kathryn Newton heads this surprisingly smart Lord of the Flies riff about a group of teenagers forced to create their own community after all the adults disappear and a dense new forest crops up around their small enclave, cutting them off from everything and everyone else. This one's about coming of age in a world where the usual rules are no longer in effect, and about how we're quick to reestablish an oppressive social order even when outside forces are no longer at work. Stream The Society on Netflix.

#3559. Why GTA 6 Doesn’t Let You Replay Missions–It Felt “Alien And Disconnected”

One of the first things people noticed with Grand Theft Auto 6 is that you cannot replay missions, at least not in a simple, straightforward way. GTA 5 had a mission replay option, as did Red Dead Redemption II, so why doesn't GTA 6?

Senior design director Scott Butchard told Kotaku that Rockstar "certainly" considered a mission replay feature "early on in development." However, Butchard said, "As the game came together, it felt at odds with the story we were trying to tell and felt a bit alien and disconnected."

He went on to say replaying missions "really diminished the choices you had made."

While GTA 6 doesn't make it easy to replay missions, you still can do so by reloading an earlier GTA 6 save. Something else to know is that if you're in the middle of a mission and it's not going to plan, you can open the game menu and select retry, quit, or restart.

GTA 6 blasted off with 32.5 million sales via prepurchases alone and around $4 billion in revenue on day one. The game is only going to get bigger and sell more copies over time, and it's helping drive new PlayStation and Xbox hardware sales.

In other GTA 6 news, the actor who plays the character Mandy has reacted to people being weird online. Rockstar has also reacted to the sentiment that GTA 6 is too easy.

It's wild to think about but Survivor has been on the air for 26 years now. The competition series (which is streaming with a Paramount+ subscription) started its run back in 2000, and longtime fans are still up to date with the current Season 51. A lot has changed over the years, including Survivor's prize money, the amount of days the game lasts, and how casting works. I recently watched a vintage clip from back in Season 2, and it totally made me miss OG Jeff Probst.

The second season of the show was titled Australian Outback, and is arguably one of the best Survivor seasons in the show's long history. Some of the most iconic players ever came out of Season 2, including Jerri Manthey and the great Colby Donaldson. I recently saw a clip of a wildly dangerous challenge, and I was shook by how different the entire show feels nowadays. You can check out the video for yourself below:

A post shared by Susie Mac (@survivordeepdive)

Honestly, how crazy is this Survivor challenge? Rather than the standard ones we're used to seeing every season, the above clip shows Jeff asking the cast to jump off a cliff and try to survive floating down rapids with boxes of supplies. It's truly terrifying to watch it play out, especially when you consider that Rodger Bingham had only JUST learned to swim before starting the game.

I loved re-watching this unique challenge, as I've grown tired of seeing the same ones every single season. I mean, how many times can we watch the contestants do the same puzzle? The show's early seasons used to have challenges that were themed based on their location, making each one unique. Although as we know, Survivor has been permanently based in Fiji since Season 33. So the location-based theming has been gone since 2016.

Seeing this retro Survivor clip also made me miss the OG version of host Jeff Probst. While he's pretty warm and cuddly nowadays, he used to be more of a hard ass. I used to love hearing him throw shade at the contestants, often adding salt to fresh wounds in the process. Seriously, he used to call people or tribes "completely useless" back in the day. This always cracked me up, but nowadays the host/showrunner is more likely to give folks a warm hug.

Jeff used to be scary during classic Survivor, but that's simply not the vibe anymore. I mean, castaways are so comfortable around him they're willing to interrupt his speeches and even give him a nickname like "Uncle Jeff." Where's the respect, people?

Survivor airs new episodes Wednesdays as part of the 2026 TV schedule. We'll just have to see if Probst ends up changing his tune at all throughout the rest of Season 51.

#3556. Another Live-Service Game Is Going Extinct, And This One Has Dinosaurs

Capcom has had a big year, but amid the hits comes news that its Overwatch-with-dinosaurs game, Exoprimal, will join the live-service graveyard next year. The game's servers will go offline next year, making it unplayable after that.

"Thank you so much for your continued use of Exoprimal, a statement on the Exoprimal site reads. "We regret to announce that service for Exoprimal will be discontinued as of Thursday, September 30, 2027. We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement."

Exoprimal season passes are no longer available to purchase through storefronts, and Capcom will slowly wind down the game over several months. Exoprimal and all its DLC will be delisted from stores starting March 30, 2027, but anyone who owns it can still download and play it before the September 2027 deadline. Despite a cool premise and fun gameplay, Exoprimal never truly took off after its 2023 launch.

"While Exoprimal’s early hours of repetitive and simple missions will likely drive some people away, its later surprises are a delight for those willing to give it the necessary time," James Carr wrote in GameSpot's Exoprimal review. "The escalation of difficulty and the wide variety of objectives introduced later on in the shooter gives it fresh life several hours in. Fighting through an ocean of dinosaurs is a ton of fun, and the variety of enemies keeps you from falling into a repetitive combat loop."

The writing was already on the wall for Exoprimal in 2024, as Capcom announced it was ending seasonal updates and would rotate through existing content on a monthly schedule. While that doesn't reflect the entire player community, Exoprimal numbers have largely cratered on PC via Steam: it peaked at 4,9995 concurrent players in November 2023 and nosedived the following month. At the time of writing, Exoprimal's 24-hour peak was a paltry 23 players.

2026 has been merciless for live-service games, with several high-profile casualties. Developer Wildlight’s free-to-play shooter Highguard quickly lost momentum after its January launch, Anthem was sunset this year, and New World: Aeternum began winding down operations ahead of its January 2027 closure.

#3555. Decoding Kate Middleton’s “Tourdrobe” for Her Trip to India

When Kate Middleton stepped out on the green carpet at the Earthshot Awards ceremony in Mumbai this week, it was “an absolute princess moment,” says British designer Amanda Wakeley.

“Catherine has really come into her own. She has found her stride and a new confidence, and you see that in this dazzling but also practical ‘tourdrobe,’’’ Wakeley, who has previously dressed the Princess of Wales and used to dress Princess Diana, tells Vanity Fair.

It has been 10 years since Princess Kate last visited India. Her fashion choices are more sophisticated now than on her visit in 2016, and the speech she delivered at the Earthshot Prize ceremony on November 17 shows a new confidence. With her elevated look, there’s no trace of High Street labels. Kate’s flared floral dresses and the wedge shoes she used to love (but the late Queen Elizabeth apparently disliked) have been replaced by Manolo Blahnik pumps, couture power suits, and clothes by some of her favorite designers, such as Emilia Wickstead.

Prince William and Princess Kate attend The Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

Kate’s decision to wear a striking vermilion dress made from handwoven silk by New Delhi–based designer Mahima Mahajan to the Earthshot Prize ceremony spoke volumes. The eye-catching dress, which she paired with a burgundy Prada velvet clutch, was chosen after Kate had selected a special suite of emeralds from the royal gem collection. The green stones on the dress perfectly matched her jewels, which served as an homage to both Queen Elizabeth II and India, as the green of the Indian flag represents growth and prosperity.

The dazzling stones known as the “emerald tassel suite” were worn frequently by the late Queen Elizabeth II, and while Kate has previously worn the earrings, this marked the first time she wore the set. The effect was dramatic.

“Never has Catherine looked more like a queen in waiting,” Wakeley says of the look.

Wearing the suite ensured that Kate, who has free rein of the royal jewels, looked more regal than ever. “What was fascinating was seeing Catherine wear these incredible family heirlooms along with more relaxed collections from some of her favorite modern jewelry designers like Kiki McDonough and Astley Clarke,” remarks Wakeley.

Kate’s carefully curated wardrobe for the trip wasn’t just about power dressing—it was also about showing she can be sustainable as well as on trend.

“It was good to see Catherine making a proper nod to sustainability by rewearing her Roksanda dress,” Wakeley notes. “It’s clear a lot of thought has gone into her outfit choices. Her wardrobe has to be practical, and her clothes have to work harder than most people consider for their clothing; she needs weight in the hem of the floaty dresses. She has learned lessons the hard way. She is often seen bending down, talking to children, so she’s conscious of how low a neckline is, how short a skirt is.”

Princess Kate visits the Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital, on November 18, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

For her visit to Mumbai’s Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital on November 18, Catherine chose a striking red tailored Emilia Wickstead skirt suit with Manolo Blahnik pumps. On November 16, she opted for a pistachio blazer by designer Veronica Beard, paired with white Alexander McQueen trousers and pearl-buckled Camilla Elphick flats, a relaxed and accessible look for when she picked up a cricket bat.

Princess Kate plays cricket on November 16, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

As Princess of Wales, Catherine is often compared to Princess Diana. “The main difference is Diana was a fashion icon. Catherine has become a style icon,” Wakeley says. “There’s a big difference. Diana played into the fashion of the day and was finding her style. During the time she resigned from public life, she worked out her style DNA. Catherine has had to do that on the job. Very wisely, she has worked out her style and doesn’t get too impacted by fashion and trends. She goes for what she likes. What works for her rather than trends. She really knows now what works for her.”

#3554. If You Loved 'Cupertino,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

Jeff Somers is a freelancer who has been writing about writing, books, personal finance, and home maintenance since 2012.

Jeff has published nine novels and more than 70 short stories; his story Ringing the Changes was selected for inclusion in The Best American Mystery Stories 2006. In 2018, Jeff published the book Writing Without Rules: How to Write & Sell a Novel Without Guidelines, Experts, or (Occasionally) Pants. He holds a bachelor’s degree in English and previously worked in medical publishing as a production editor.

When not writing, Jeff spends his free time fixing up his old house. He has tackled a wide range of DIY projects, including remodeling a bathroom entirely on his own in two weeks, and building a roof deck that hasn't fallen down yet. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

Cupertino is one of those TV shows that arrived just when we all needed it. In this economy, a story about two lawyers who get shafted by the “move fast and break things” culture of Silicon Valley and decide to use their legal chops to fight back was almost destined to be a hit, and the great performances by Mike Colter and Rachel Keller sealed the deal. If you love the sharp legal wrangling and tech-focused storylines and want a movie that perfectly complements the show, it’s time to watch (or re-watch) Aaron Sorkin and David Fincher’s 2010 masterpiece, The Social Network.

Just like Cupertino, The Social Network arrived at precisely the right moment in history—just when everyone was beginning to wonder if the social media revolution kicked off by Facebook and Mark Zuckerberg was actually a good idea or not. While it might seem hard to imagine, there was a time when Facebook was the social media platform—everyone was on it, and it dominated the conversation like nothing else. And the outsized wealth and influence Zuckerberg accrued as a result were just starting to make people a little uneasy.

At its core, The Social Network is a legal drama—the framing narrative involves dual lawsuits brought against Zuckerberg and the depositions he is giving, which prompt flashbacks to the formation and success of Facebook in the early 2000s. Like Cupertino, the story is soaked in the “apologize later” culture of tech startups, and traces the ruthlessness and cold genius of Zuckerberg as he cements his control over the platform, ices out former partners, and generally behaves like a sociopathic genius (Jesse Eisenberg’s performance as Zuckerberg is coldly compelling).

The film doesn’t have any kind of clear-cut ending where the good guys win, but there’s a certain satisfaction in the way Sorkin’s script and Eisenberg’s performance strip away the glamour of Zuckerberg’s money and success, reducing him in many ways to an aggrieved loner who translated his rage into a brilliant idea, and then has to isolate himself from everyone in order to maintain his control over it. The Zuckerberg depicted in the film is a lonely, bitter dude, and it’s as much of a happy ending as you’ll get. It’s a fascinating story of legal maneuvering and bickering lawyers against a backdrop of one of the foundational social media moments that shaped modern culture, and fans of the show will dig it. Stream The Social Network on Pluto or rent it on Prime Video.

Still craving legal drama, tech-sector skulduggery, or more David-versus-Goliath courtroom fireworks? Here are a few more movies that fans of Cupertino will love.

It’s set nowhere near Silicon Valley, but Michael Clayton is a real barn-burner of a paranoid legal thriller. George Clooney plays the title role, a “fixer” for a big-money law firm. When his mentor and friend, Arthur Edens (Tom Wilkinson), suffers a mental breakdown while working on a case involving a toxic weedkiller produced by one of the firm’s clients and becomes a security threat, he’s assassinated, and Clayton is forced to reckon with his role in the world and how much injustice he’s willing to tolerate in exchange for money. It’s tense, smart, and has a wonderfully satisfying conclusion that fans of legal dramas where the good guys are willing to sacrifice (and win) will cheer. Rent Michael Clayton on Prime Video.

Based on real events, Dark Waters will appeal to anyone who likes to see smart lawyers take on enormous corporations in a search for the truth. A successful corporate lawyer, Robert Bilott (Mark Ruffalo), looks into a series of bizarre cattle deaths in rural West Virginia and stumbles onto evidence that the DuPont corporation has been dumping illegal, unregulated chemicals into the groundwater. Bilott’s years-long effort to hold DuPont responsible for the health impact on the community nearly costs him everything, but his determination to make the system work is ultimately the kind of inspiring legal story fans of Cupertino will appreciate. Rent Dark Waters on Prime Video.

If you just want the simple pleasures of a thrilling legal procedural, you can’t do much better than A Civil Action. John Travolta (at the height of his comeback) plays attorney Jan Schlichtmann, who takes on a class action lawsuit against two huge corporations because he thinks the case will be lucrative and relatively straightforward. As the case saps his resources and brings his firm to the brink of collapse, however, Schlichtmann slowly realizes that he’s fighting for more than just a big payday. Fair warning: This isn’t a feel-good movie in many ways, but it definitely brings those David-versus-Goliath vibes that Cupertino trades in. Rent A Civil Action on Prime Video.

The true story behind the effort to license the video game Tetris from the Soviet-era Russian government doesn’t have the same stakes as many of the stories in Cupertino, and it’s certainly no longer timely. But the globe-trotting legal maze that Henk Rogers (Taron Egerton) must navigate to secure the rights, which seem to keep twisting and slipping from his grasp as various political and corporate interests weigh in, is just as fun and fascinating as the legal battles on the show. Tetris may no longer be a novel sensation in the gaming world, but it’s fascinating to see how something so baked into modern pop culture achieved that status. Stream Tetris on Apple TV or rent it on Prime Video.

If your favorite part of Cupertino is its exploration of the way tech companies impact our lives, and the way decisions made in obscure corporate offices can have enormous consequences, BlackBerry will be a favorite. Based on true events, it tells the story of how Research in Motion (RIM) created what was, for a time, the most dominant phone in the world—and how the company lost everything when its leaders took their eye off the ball and let personal obsessions and grudges impede their work. With a cast that includes Jay Baruchel and Glenn Howerton, this story of Silicon Valley hubris is right on target for Cupertino fans. Stream Blackberry on Netflix, Kanopy, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

#3553. Diablo 4’s Most Nostalgic Season Is Becoming (Mostly) Permanent

Diablo 4 is gearing up for the arrival of Season 16, but it won't be leaving its popular previous season behind entirely.

As detailed by Blizzard in a breakdown of the upcoming Season of Tyrael's Gambit, much of the previous season, Hell's Legacy, will become a permanent part of Diablo 4 going forward. Season 15 served as celebration of the franchise's history, and added a smorgasbord of items and callbacks to previous Diablo titles, including a storyline revolving around Deckard Cain and the return of enemies and boss encounters from Diablo 2. 

Most of that is carrying forward, Blizzard said. Due to "overwhelming requests" from the game's community, Blizzard outlined what all from Hell's Legacy will survive.

Hell's Legacy's capstone dungeons will be added, as will the ability to summon a World Boss version of Diablo and take on the cow god Moopisto. The Prime Evil Council is also becoming permanent, and will work the same way the game's other Lair bosses do, with players needing a specific item to open their reward chest after successfully defeating the encounter.

Waking Nightmare dungeons will still be accessible, but only by finding Chronicle of Nightmares dungeon keys. Monsters from previous Diablo games will also have a chance to spawn in The Pit. Those who progressed their secret cow level journey can also rejoice, as the secret cow island and its corresponding waypoint will be staying.

Many of Hell's Legacy's best items were new versions of classics from older Diablo games, and those Legacy Uniques will be added permanently as well, including the Annihilus Seal and Hellfire Torch Charm.

That's all for now, but Blizzard said more of Hell's Legacy could make a return in the future.

"Other popularly requested features are being evaluated for rework and may appear in the future," Blizzard said.

Diablo 4 Season 16 launches December 1. In addition to bringing forward much of Hell's Legacy, Tyrael's Gambit will additionally overhaul the game's War Plans system and make its Helltide activity easier.

Diablo 4 won't receive new expansions going forward, but it is receiving a new class, the Amazon, next year. Blizzard is also hard at work on Diablo 5. Though it's not slated to arrive until 2029, Blizzard has already revealed three of Diablo 5's playable classes and promised it will launch with more class options than any previous Diablo game.

#3552. 49ers’ Kyle Juszczyk Opens Up About Mother-in-Law’s Death: ‘A Strong Woman’

San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk will have his late mother-in-law on his mind when he hits the field against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, November 29.

Kyle, 35, will honor his wife Kristin’s late mom, Gini, with his custom cleats on Sunday, in partnership with Novartis’ “My Cause My Cleats” campaign. Gini died of breast cancer when Kristin, 32, was in high school.

“I didn’t have the chance to meet her,” Kyle exclusively told Us. “When Kristin is speaking about breast cancer awareness and all the partnerships that she’s done, it brings up a time for Kristin to talk about her and to tell me about her memories with her mother and for me to see what a strong woman she was.”

Kyle continued, “As a teenager, Kristin wasn’t even aware of all her mother was going through. I know as she gets older, she gets more and more information from her father about all of these different doctors she was seeing, all these different things she was trying. For Kristin and I to be aware of it just shows the strength Gini had.”

Kristin and Kyle got married in July 2019. The NFL star’s cleats will support the Lynne Cohen Foundation, which prevents breast and ovarian cancer through early detection, genetic counseling and community-based care.

Kyle further explained that the cause is “near and dear to his heart” because one of his aunts is a breast cancer survivor.

“I just know what this can do to a family,” Kyle said. “I’ve seen the effect it’s had on my wife. Any little bit of help I can throw out there — any bit of awareness about getting early screening, early detection, how you can save lives — I’m really excited to.”

This holiday season, the 49ers schedule allowed for Kyle and Kristin to host Thanksgiving at their home in California, which included all of Kyle’s family flying in from his home state of Ohio.

“It’s become a tradition that we’ve done for a number of years now because it’s tough in the NFL,” Kyle explained. “You miss so many holidays. The amount of Christmases and Thanksgivings that I’ve missed is too much to count.”

He continued, “But even if our schedule doesn’t line up for the actual week of Thanksgiving, we’ll always celebrate it. Whether it’s a week or two before, a week or two after. We make it a priority because Thanksgiving is my favorite holiday.”

The 49ers host the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, November 29, at 4:25 p.m. ET.

As Christmas inches closer, fans are getting more into the spirit thanks to the 2026 Christmas movie schedule. Hallmark once again offers a large variety of classics and has over two dozen new holiday films this year. A massive number of people have already been watching Countdown to Christmas. However, the network’s beloved lineup does not just include the main channel. Hallmark’s Christmas classics have also made their way to Hallmark+. I love the holiday films, and there are two great ones that you can only watch on streaming, for the most part, that is.

Get in on this Black Friday deal through Amazon to save big on your first three months and watch all the best Christmas and other holiday movies the streamer has to offer. Including movies that are only available on Hallmark+.

Now that Thanksgiving is over, fans are looking forward to the holiday season. And to get into the Christmas spirit, if you haven’t already, Hallmark’s Countdown to Christmas is just the thing. Of course, while the network has been showing Christmas movies 24/7 for several weeks now, Hallmark+ has even more to watch. And that means even more movies that actors have had to film during the summer. For Black Friday, fans can sign up for just $2.99 for the first three months (perfect for those upcoming cold winter nights). That includes many Hallmark series and movies, as well as exclusive originals only available on Hallmark+. After those three months, it's either $8.99 per month or $79.99 per year, and it includes plenty of great offers.

As previously mentioned, there are a handful of originals exclusively for Hallmark+, such as the When Calls the Heart prequel Hope Valley: 1874, which is coming back for Season 2. This includes the four-movie Unwrapping Christmas collection that premiered back in November 2024. Even though they premiered two years ago, the movies definitely still hold up, and two of them are arguably the best in the series.

Unwrapping Christmas follows four friends working at a gift-wrapping shop leading up to the town’s Christmas gala. Similar to The Wedding Veil series, each movie centers on a different friend and their Christmas romance. The first one, Unwrapping Christmas: Tina’s Miracle, stars Natalie Hall as the titular Tina Mitchell, the owner of said gift-wrapping shop. She finds herself in a bind after the Christmas gala she’s planning is nearly canceled until she teams up with an estate company owner to save the venue.

Of course, Hallmark is no stranger to plots about saving a business or building in time for the holidays. And the network has been criticized for being too formulaic. That being said, Tina’s Miracle is still a great watch because it sets up the rest of the movies and her own love life. She’s hesitant to open up because of a past breakup, but ultimately, she and Michael (Alec Santos) team up to save the historic venue Alford House. With some twists and turns included, it’s perfect.

The second and third movies, Mia’s Prince with Kathryn Davis and Lily’s Destiny with Ashley Newbrough, are definitely fun watches and can get anyone into the spirit. However, I do love the fourth movie, Olivia’s Reunion, which sees gift-wrapping expert Olivia (Cindy Busby) getting snowed in with her ex while delivering gifts ahead of the gala. I am a sucker for a good enemies-to-lovers plot, especially if said enemies were previously together. Putting the characters in a closed space for an undisclosed amount of time, you never know what could happen. Plus, Jake Epstein, who plays the ex, has a soft spot in my heart after portraying Craig Manning on Degrassi: The Next Generation.

All four Unwrapping Christmas movies ultimately premiered on Hallmark Channel in July 2025, but seeing that they are Hallmark+ exclusives, I couldn’t help but relive them. Fans can relive those movies and plenty more Hallmark favorites on Hallmark+. Countdown to Christmas is far from over, and there is a movie for everyone.

#3550. Three Years After His Death, EA Is Using AI To Bring Back A Famed Commentator In FC 27

EA Sports FC 27 is adding an AI-generated commentator for the first time in the series' history, with famed British commentator John Motson having his voice synthesized for the football title.

Motson, who passed way in 2023, previously provided commentary for EA's FIFA series, appearing in the game's first iteration in 1996 and featuring until 2005. According to the BBC, EA approached Motson's wife and son for permission to regenerate his voice and use his likeness for this year's entry in the series. Both agreed to the idea, but neither party has disclosed how much EA has paid for the use. Fred Motson, John's son, stated that he believed his father would've approved of this use of AI.

"My dad was the least technological person in the world," Fred stated. "Till his dying day, he had a typewriter on his desk. So I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically, but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects."

Peter Caulfield, founder of Save Our Voices Now, which campaigns against this exact use of AI, questions whether a family should be able to provide consent for someone who can no longer give it themselves. "If someone has signed a deal allowing their likeness to be used after they die, I have no issue with that," he explained. "But in life or in death, unless you have specifically agreed to it, AI cloning of any kind should not be allowed. Being a family member shouldn't automatically give you that right either."

This isn't new to video games, either. Epic Games used a similar method to bring back the late James Earl Jones' voice for its Star Wars event in Fortnite, with the actor's estate agreeing to the use. It allowed players to converse with the AI bot while playing, and was very quickly removed after some users managed to get the bot to spew out racist or vulgar phrases, all delivered with the voice of Jones. It also drew the ire of SAG-AFTRA, which claimed that Epic had violated labor practices.

Derek Rae, one of the currently employed commentators on EA Sports FC 27, said he was excited by the inclusion of Motson's voice, and that he didn't believe AI was yet going to replace his own work on the game. When asked whether he would make the same decision to have his work endure for years to come through AI, he replied, "I'm hopefully many years away from having to make a decision like that."

#3548. The Best Last-Minute Gifts That Don't Feel Last Minute

This series will help you pick the perfect presents, decor, and activities to make this Christmas the Best Christmas Ever.

We’ve all experienced gift panic—that sinking feeling when you realize you need a present in an hour and you just don’t have one to give. Whether you spent all year chasing the “perfect” gift or simply procrastinated, your time is nearly up. But don’t panic. The clock may have nearly run out, but your options haven’t. Before you resort to re-gifting something from the back of a closet, here’s how to pull off a last-minute gift that is effortless but feels elevated and worthy of the person you’re giving it to.

With the right presentation, even the most last-minute gift can read as thoughtful. Any performer will tell you that the difference between a good show and a bad one comes down to commitment and confidence. The same is true for last-minute gifts: If you act like your gift is thoughtful and intentional, they’ll think it is. The biggest mistake people make is apologizing as they hand over a present—nothing ruins a vibe faster than, “Sorry this is so last-minute.” So give with confidence.

And focus on presentation. A handwritten note that contains a shared memory or personal joke can elevate a present. Use simple but personal wrapping; craft paper and twine, or a reusable gift bag that looks like you planned ahead. Add a small flourish, like a sprig of holly or a fancy bow. Small touches can make it seem like you’ve carefully prepared. What you don’t want are obvious panic gifts that scream, “I grabbed this on the way here.” The goal is effortless, not frantic.

Digital gifts are your friends. You can order something in minutes that arrives instantly online, and with a little thought, will still read as personal and intentional. The trick is choosing a present that speaks to the recipient’s tastes, hobbies, or quirks, and pairing it with a small note to show you remember what they love. From e-books to streaming subscriptions, these gifts hit the sweet spot of thoughtful and last-minute. Here are some suggestion:

When time is running out, gift cards are your secret weapon. They arrive instantly online, don’t require shipping, and with the right presentation, they can feel surprisingly thoughtful. The key is to pick a card that fits the recipient’s interests and add a personal note. The more specific you are, the better. If your giftee is into Italian food, get them an Eataly gift card. If they're a PC gamer, get them a Steam card. If they're into education, a membership to Skillshare is perfect. There's a gift card out there for just about any interest, and all you have to do it google it and email it.

Generic gift cards can be a last-minute lifesaver that can still seem a little personal if you give them the right way.

Pick a theme or design: Many online cards, like Amazon, Etsy, or Starbucks, let you choose designs. The right visual makes the card feel more intentional.

Include a warm, personal message: Even one line can make a digital card feel thoughtful—something like, “I couldn’t pick just one thing for you. Hope this helps you treat yourself.”

Send strategically: Deliver the card by email or text, but consider printing the email or screenshotting it in a small envelope so it feels like a “real” gift.

Sign someone up for a subscription service, write a note explaining you want to keep giving them presents all year, and you're golden. Here are some suggestions:

SnackCrate: This service sends a different snack from around the world every month.

SpiceClub: For the culinary adventurer on your list. A subscription to RawSpiceBar’s Spice Club delivers a curated selection of spices every month.

Mocktail Club: Booze-free fancy drinks delivered once a month? Sign me up.

Thera Box: If you know someone in need of some self-care, this once-a-month box is packed with wellness and relaxation items.

Loot Crate: If your giftee is geeky, consider this monthly surprise box of pop culture treasures.

Cameo is a platform where celebrities, influencers, musicians, and performers create personalized video messages for fans. If someone on your list is a fan of someone on Cameo, you can set up a session, and give a card with a mysterious note like "Keep an eye out for a special message." They'll be delighted with a personal message from wrestling legend Mick Foley or terrified when Chris Hansen appears on their screen; your choice.

I have enough crap in my house, so I love getting experiences instead of things. The challenge with experience gifts is usually timing: Many require reservations or coordination, but there are plenty of options that let your giftee schedule the time, making them perfect last-minute gifts.

Museum membership cards: Many institutions sell digital gift memberships that the recipient can activate whenever they like.

Movie tickets: Your local multiplex probably has a gift certificate you can buy online.

Local attraction passes: Some city attractions offer gift cards or “anytime admission” tickets that don’t expire immediately.

Pair these with a note explaining why you chose the experience, or, if you have that kind of relationship, something like, "I want to take you to the Museum of Modern Art." Just make sure you follow through and actually go.

Sometimes, there’s literally no time to order, wrap, or even think about a gift. If you’re scrambling out the door and need something now, you might be able to fake your way through, even if you're stopping at the liquor store on the way to the Christmas party.

Flowers or a small potted plant: Give a seasonal bouquet or a small indoor plant. Add a handwritten note, even a single line, and it might come off as thoughtful.

Gourmet chocolates or candy: Specialty chocolates from a local shop or grocery store display can feel luxe with a little ribbon or bag.

Wine, craft beer, or non-alcoholic beverage: A bottle with a clean label or interesting packaging immediately elevates your gift. Ask the clerk at the liquor store to help you find something unique.

Lottery tickets: Who wouldn't appreciate a bunch of scratch-off lottery tickets?

Hard cash is the most impersonal gift of all, but the only one you know will be used. This gift really depends on the person getting it, so be aware of whether they're likely to think "Just what I wanted!" or "Wait, I'm not poor." If you give cash, make sure it's crisp bills in a nice card, with a personalized note.

#3546. Mario, Pikachu, And Other Gaming Icon Balloons Won’t Be Flying This Thanksgiving

New York City is no stranger to bad weather, be it blazing-hot summers, snow-packed winters, or fierce windstorms. Unfortunately for countless families who have made it a holiday tradition to turn on the TV and watch giant totems of pop culture sail in the streets of the great city, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been officially delayed due to a forecast of rain and windstorms--a first in its 100-year history.

In recent years, gaming icons have become more and more prominent during the parade. Beginning in 1993, a balloon of Sonic the Hedgehog marked the first game character to float among the procession. Since then, more characters have joined the festivities, including Mario, Pac-Man, Pikachu, and even Red the Angry Bird, among others.

However, those who have followed the history of Macy's balloons know that the mix of bad weather and massive, floating objects can result in genuine danger for balloon handlers, bystanders, and objects on the streets. Rather infamously, Sonic's 1993 appearance was marred by an incident where the balloon got stuck on a lamppost, popping the balloon and injuring two bystanders.

Other balloon bursts have proved even more catastrophic, with a series of mishaps in 1997 leading to a Cat in the Hat balloon causing injuries that left a woman comatose for days. Since then, more emphasis has rightfully been put on safety.

While it might be disappointing to not be able to point at the TV and go "Mario!" with your younger cousins around the TV tomorrow, the balloons will get a chance to fly on Saturday starting at 8:30 AM ET, when the weather is likely to be significantly less awful. You can find other ways to fill the time--but maybe ask your relatives first if it's okay to let the kiddos watch you play GTA 6.

#3544. GTA 6’s Furry Rescue Mission Is A Little Weird, But The Rewards Are Worth It

No matter what you do in GTA 6, it pales in comparison to being a Furry in that game. Anyone looking to externalize their inner animal spirit is in danger of being hunted, and you'll find out for yourself just how much the fictional state of Leonida hates Furries when you're given the chance to save one of them from being murdered by the cops. Should you help them? Absolutely, if you want an easy payday or a new weapon for your arsenal.

How to find Chase the Fox

Like several other missions in GTA 6, helping out the Furry resistance appears to trigger randomly. The mission takes place after Chapter 3, on Miramar Drive in Crosstown, Vice City, and you'll want to be cruising around that area at night, between midnight and 4 AM.

Once it starts, you'll see cops pull up to hunt down a Furry by the name of Chase, and if you drive up to him, you can either give him a lift or leave him to his brutal fate.

Outrun the cops

If you do choose to help Chase, then get ready to be hunted down by cops. You'll pick up a three-star Wanted level, which means the cops will be in mildly hot pursuit of your vehicle.

Reach the parking garage

Chase will direct you to a nearby parking garage, where his Furry allies are waiting. After a short standoff, they'll welcome you into their ranks as an honorary Furry.

Courier the group to safety

To get the law off your polyester tail, one of your new allies will take your car and use it to distract the cops. Get inside the van, and you can bring the other Furries home to their swanky pad in Starfish Island. While you're driving, the Furries will interact with each other, and you can watch their hijinks.

Choose your reward

Once Chase and his pals are back home, you'll be offered one of two rewards: $15,000 in cash or the unique Furry DW-9 submachine gun. Personally, I'd go with the gun since it's easy enough to make cash in GTA 6, and having more weapons is never a bad idea. You'll also gain safehouse access to the Furry group's hideout, where you can stock up on weapons and body armor.

For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

#3542. Man Arrested for Allegedly Stabbing Double Amputee Girlfriend in Brutal Attack

A Florida man has been accused of stabbing his double amputee girlfriend – who uses a wheelchair – in a brutal attack, leaving her to suffer several severe injuries.

The woman was stabbed around 11 p.m. on Tuesday, November 24, in her home in Miami, Florida, according to a Miami-Dade county criminal complaint obtained by Us.

Before she was intubated, the woman identified her boyfriend, Marcos Enrique Sanchezpaz, as the person who attacked her. Sanchezpaz, 42, fled the scene, but he was later arrested when he returned to the residence.

An investigation was launched into the matter, and authorities learned that the incident escalated after the couple got into an argument. Sanchezpaz allegedly grabbed a knife and stabbed the woman several times.

The woman fell out of her wheelchair and managed to FaceTime her son while lying on the ground. “My boyfriend stabbed me,” she reportedly told her son, per police.

The victim then made the same claim to officers when they reported to the scene of the crime. Before she was transported to the hospital, she reportedly said, “My boyfriend stabbed me.”

The woman sustained multiple lacerations to her torso, her spleen and her chest area during the attack. Additionally, she suffered broken ribs and experienced bleeding in her lungs. Authorities said that was intubated as she was being taken to the hospital.

The victim’s current condition is not known as of time of publication.

Authorities said that Sanchezpaz fled the scene after he stabbed the woman, though he later returned. Police noted that he seemingly had blood on his shoe.

Police said Sanchezpaz was incoherent and he was taken to a hospital for evaluation. Once he was checked out, he was transferred to a jail.

Sanchezpaz has since been charged with one count of attempted murder, according to his online court records. The defendant has pleaded not guilty to the charge, and it’s not currently clear if he has retained legal counsel following his arrest.

Authorities confirmed that the couple had been in a relationship for about two years. However, they did not reveal if the couple has a history of domestic violence.

The Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office had no additional information to share about the case when contacted by Us about updates.

#3541. Rockstar Games Has A GTA 6 Hit On Its Hands, But Its Union Vote Is A Loss

Roughly 75% of Rockstar Games staff in the UK have voted against a formal recognition agreement with the Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB). The news came in the wake of GTA 6's record-breaking launch, and had the IWGB been recognized, Rockstar Games management would have been legally obligated to negotiate collective bargaining terms with the union on topics such as pay, hours, and conditions.

Voting took place across two weeks, and turnout was massive, with over 93% of UK staff casting their ballot (roughly 1,544 employees). The IWGB said it was undeterred by the result and would continue working to build support among Rockstar employees. "While the result means Rockstar will not be formally required to hold regular meetings with union representatives under a recognition agreement, it does not prevent workers from continuing to organize and push for workplace improvements through the IWGB, joining the union or exercising their individual trade union rights and protections," the union said in a statement.

The vote also comes hot on the heels of the IWGB taking Rockstar to an employment tribunal, alleging unlawful dismissal and union busting after it fired over 30 employees last year for gross misconduct over alleged leaks of confidential information. Closing submissions were wrapped up shortly before the vote results came out, and a ruling is still pending. While game dev unionizing has gained significant momentum over the years, a decisive loss at one of the industry's biggest studios could be a notable speed bump for union organizers.

With Rockstar also riding the wave of GTA 6's monumental success, employees may be focused on bonuses and post-launch momentum, which could make pushing through a formal union structure even harder. "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society--this isn't a sign to retreat; it's a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues,' the IWGB added.

Major spoilers for the Blade Runner 2099 finale, “Share the Fantasy” lie ahead.

Blade Runner 2099 has finally arrived, delivering eight dystopian and drama-filled installments that deftly build upon the mythology of the beloved sci-fi franchise. The show follows dying Replicant Blade Runner Olwen (played by Michelle Yeoh) and desperate Replicant imitator Cora (Hunter Schafer), who eventually uncover a long-held secret regarding the Tyrell Corporation. This all culminates into quite a finale, and Schafer and series creator Silka Luisa spoke to CinemaBlend about THAT final Cora scene.

Ahead of “Share the Fantasy,” Cora has learned that her adoptive mother, Helena (Sheila Atim) was actually a Nexus-1 Replicant, who was killed by fellow Nexus 1 model Julius (Tom Burke). It turns out the memory belongs to Replicant creator Eldon Tyrell and holds the process of producing the (longer living) Nexus-1s. Olwen and Cora head to an Tyrell Off-World Launch complex, where the former wants to receive more time to live and the latter aims to get the memory back from Julius, who wants the sole power to create Replicants.

Ultimately, Julius destroys the memory and is killed shortly after by his bloodthirsty cohort, Clotilde (Amy Lennox), who he transformed into a Nexus-1 and left in the dark about certain details. Amid the chaos, Cora is also seriously injured and seemingly near death. Clotilde then reveals to Olwen that she knows how to produce Nexus-1s and offers it to Olwen to repay her for saving her life earlier. While someone is later turned into a Nexus-1, it’s unclear who it is, as viewers only see a hand coming out of a pod.

In the final scene of this 2026 TV schedule entry, Olwen is seen exploring planets off world but, before that,, Cora returns to the Replicant police station, where she undergoes another Voight-Kampff human-detection evaluation by Greta (Katelyn Rose Downey). While Cora fails, she seems more calculating and emotionally tests Greta with her own responses. It’s a well-acted and complex scene, so I had to ask the creative team about it.

Needless to say, the Cora scene – like the finale as a whole – leaves viewers with a lot to chew on. Showrunner Silka Luisa, a longtime fan of the Blade Runner franchise, wouldn’t give any specific answers about the last moment with Cora. However, during her conversation with CinemaBlend, she did acknowledge her thoughts on why viewers would likely have differing thoughts about it:

Blade Runner always has an ambiguous ending, and so I think part of what I'm really proud of in the show is that you come to the end and that people can have different interpretations about what that final scene means to them, and they can imagine, just like you asked me on 2049…. They can fill in that with their own story.

While 2099 doesn’t have any direct ties to the events of the films, it does indeed follow in their footsteps by providing an ambiguous ending. So I completely agree with Luisa that it’ll spark differing interpretations from viewers. And, just as I probed Luisa for her take on Rick Deckard’s post-2049 fate, I also directly asked whether Cora would just masquerade as a Replicant moving forward. The EP would only say this to me:

We can't answer that question, but I can tell [you] I loved writing it. But I mean, [Hunter and I] didn't even talk that much about it. Hunter just came on set, and she felt so different. I mean, you just came on and just nailed it. It was one of those things where I like, my jaw hit the floor. She's so phenomenal in that scene.

There’s so much to consider in the scene, including the notion that Cora may have actually undergone the Nexus-1 process and become a Replicant herself. Alas, Schafer avoided giving any specifics on that, but she did speak highly of her experience filming the scene and how it differed from much of her time on set:

I loved that scene because it — well, I mean, also at that point in filming, like by Episode 8, you know, I'm not really having to think too much about character work anymore at that point. She's in me, and I can just sort of drop into her. I love when you reach that point in filming, but it was fun because it felt like a different Cora in a different sort of energetic place. And so I think we just had fun filming it. Also, [director] Ariel [Kleiman] was super down to play with it. Yeah, I mean, it's hard to talk about. It's so wild talking about it now.

This show succeeds in delivering impressive visuals, strong performances and brutal action, though I also applaud Silka Luisa and her staff for adding some fresh elements to the franchise. And, while I would love to have some concrete answers regarding the final moments of this limited series, a part of me certainly respects Luisa’s desire to let the audience made up their own mind about the finer details.

#3539. Nintendo's Black Friday Deals Are Actually Pretty Good

Black Friday is nearly upon us. From now through Cyber Monday, retailers and companies alike are offering deals and discounts on their wares. While I always keep an eye out for Nintendo deals offered by stores like Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart, it seems the company is offering its own discounts this year—and, surprisingly, they're actually pretty solid.

Last Thursday, Nintendo announced its Black Friday discounts. We've already seen Switch 2 sales ahead of the Black Friday season, but now, Nintendo has confirmed an official discount for the console.

Starting Nov. 22 through Dec. 5, you can pick up Nintendo's Switch 2 Mario Kart bundle for $499.00, down $50 from $549.99. That includes the console, a download of Mario Kart World, and a 90-day Nintendo Switch Online Individual Membership.

If you already have a Switch 2 console and/or Mario Kart World, you're not left out of the Black Friday deals here. From Nov. 22 through Nov. 29, Nintendo is also running discounts on several high-profile Switch and Switch 2 games:

Donkey Kong Bananza was one of Nintendo's launch titles for the Switch 2. And while it's been out for over a year, Donkey Kong's first 3D game is still among the best-reviewed titles on the console. Nintendo is taking $20 off the game's MSRP for this promotion.

Kirby Air Riders on Switch 2 is only the second installment in the series. The original launched all the way back on the GameCube, and while the title typically runs for $69.99, Nintendo is letting it go for $49.99.

Metroid Prime 4 arrived last year after an 18-year wait from Metroid Prime 3: Corruption. The game typically retails for $69.99 for a physical copy on Switch 2, but Nintendo is selling it for $49 during its early Black Friday promotion.

Super Mario Galaxy (both the original and the sequel) are beloved by fans. These titles originally launched on the Wii, and Nintendo rereleased both for the Switch. (The company offers a free upgrade to the Switch 2 edition.) Nintendo asks $69.99 for this combo, and while you can find it for under $60, you'll officially be able to pick it up for $48.97 before Black Friday.

Nintendo's latest Mario Party, Jamboree, has a Switch 2 edition with a rather staggering MSRP of $79.99. While it's the version of the game with the most features, it's also the most expensive. You'll be able to buy it for $39.99 for Black Friday, saving up to $40.

Nintendo rarely offers official discounts on some of its biggest titles, especially in this current era. In addition, Nintendo announced a sale on its digital store that runs from Nov. 19 through Dec. 2, though it didn't say which titles would be on sale. Just keep an eye on all these dates: The Switch 2 console promotion runs longer than the physical and digital games discounts, while the digital sale runs longer than the physical sale. Nintendo says that these discounts will be available "at select retailers," as well as its brick-and-mortar locations in New York and San Francisco. You can also buy the Switch 2 bundle through Nintendo's website.

It depends! Its Nintendo Switch 2 bundle deal runs from Nov. 22 through Dec. 5; the select games listed above will be on sale from Nov. 22 through Nov. 29; and digital titles will have discounts from Nov. 19 through Dec. 2.

While we don't know which digital titles will be discounted yet, we do know that physical copies of Donkey Kong Bananza, Kirby Air Riders, Metroid Prime 4: Beyond, Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2, and Super Mario Party: Jamboree will be on sale for $39.99 each.

Yes! The Switch 2 alone costs $499.99, so you essentially get the game for free. Mario Kart World is also one of the console's best multiplayer titles right now, so it makes sense to pick it up in this bundle.

Released in 2024, it’s a co-op survival-horror game that throws a team of up to four players into a gauntlet of deadly trials, where evasion is key to victory. You can also play it solo, and if the onslaught of festive season cheerfulness is getting to you, then this will be a nice–but brutal–change of pace.

If you’d prefer to focus on the coziness of the season, then Hela: Of Mice and Magic looks like a fun time. Set in a magical forest inspired by Scandinavian lands, the game follows a group of mice on a journey to help people, at the behest of an old witch who can’t make the trip herself. This is also a day-one release for Xbox Game Pass, and it’ll be joined by World of Tanks Blitz on the same day. On December 3, Freestyle Football 2 launches, bringing fast-paced, 5v5 multiplayer street soccer to Xbox and PC, and on December 14, you can grab Nubby’s Number Factory, a roguelite game all about making big numbers.

Xbox Game Pass December Wave 1 Games

December 1

  • The Outlast Trials (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC) — Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass
  • Hela: Of Mice and Magic (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC) — Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass
  • World of Tanks Blitz

December 3

  • Freestyle Football 2

December 14

  • Nubby’s Number Factory

If you missed it, November brought a solid selection of releases. The first wave added the dungeon-crawling roguelike deck-building game Dungeon Crawlers to more Game Pass tiers, along with Warhammer Survivors and John Carpenter’s Toxic Commando. The Game Pass library expanded further later in November, with some Paw Patrol fun for the kiddos, High on Life 2, and the pretty good long-distance stealth game Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2.

#3537. Prince William Reportedly Wants to Strip Prince Harry of His Titles

Prince William is reportedly actively considering a plan for a “far-reaching restructuring” of the British monarchy, which he would implement once he ascends to the throne. His brother, Prince Harry, would be at the forefront of these changes: The future monarch reportedly wants only active members of the royal family who carry out duties on his behalf to retain their royal titles and the style of “Royal Highness.” These titles would therefore no longer be an “automatic privilege of birth” but would instead be equivalent to a “job title.”

The plan was detailed by Tom Sykes, a journalist and writer specializing in the royals, in his book Dukes of Hazard, to be published next February, excerpts of which were published by the Mail on Sunday on Saturday, November 21. The author, “a royal authority with impeccable society contacts” as the newspaper puts it, is said to have obtained confessions from friends of Prince William.

“If you are a working royal—going out, touring the country, doing diplomatic work, doing government work, having a public role, pressing the flesh, getting out of bed on a wet Wednesday to go to Sheffield—then you will be an HRH and you will have a prince or princess title. You will also get an allowance, a salary, and a place to live. One place to live,” the associate of the prince explained to Sykes. “If you are not doing those things and you are not a working royal, you will not get to be an HRH, you will not get a free or subsidized place to live, and you will not get any special favors. You will, however, be a private citizen free to get on with your life and make money any way you choose.”

By implementing this measure, Prince William hopes to prevent potential media scandals regarding the legitimacy of certain individuals’ right to retain their titles if they are not prominent members of the Firm (Prince Harry) or if they are under legal scrutiny (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor). But also, and above all, the Prince of Wales hopes to offer an option to his children, Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, eight, who could easily renounce their titles to pursue independent careers. The question does not arise for the eldest child of the Prince and Princess of Wales, Prince George, 13, whose future as heir to the throne is “guaranteed.” In fact, none of the three use their royal titles, preferring simply to be called by their first names and the surname Wales.

Under the rules established by King George V in 1917, the title of prince or princess, along with the predicate, is granted at birth to the sovereign’s children and to the children of the sovereign’s sons, as well as to all the children of the Prince of Wales’s eldest son. Prince William’s children, therefore, received these titles at birth, while Prince Harry’s children, Archie and Lilibet (ages seven and five), did not become prince and princess until King Charles III ascended the throne.

They may have to give them up if Prince William carries out his plan. “Under William’s current plan, the prince and princess titles of Harry and Meghan’s children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, would be legally removed, along with the royal styles and princely titles of Harry and Meghan themselves,” writes Tom Sykes in his book. To do so, according to Sykes’s book, constitutional advisers have told William that he could issue letters patent, an official document authorized by the king. Such a decision could strain the relationship between the two brothers.

Sykes is convinced that Prince William would garner the approval of his subjects and “enormous public support in a country increasingly impatient with the cost and perceived excess of a sprawling royal household,” according to those close to him.

In October 2025, Prince William confided to actor Eugene Levy—whom he was hosting at Windsor Castle for the taping of Levy’s show The Reluctant Traveler—that “there are points when you look at tradition and go, Is that still fit for purpose today? Is that still the right thing to do? Are we still doing and having the most impact we could be having?”

Kensington Palace, however, declined to comment on the rumor. “As a matter of policy, we don’t comment on books or claims made within them.”

#3536. 'CBS Mornings' Coanchor Gayle King's Family Guide: 2 Kids, Grandchildren, More

Gayle King‘s family has long been a focal point of her life and career, from her 1980s marriage to William Bumpus to her evolving role as a mother and grandmother.

The CBS Mornings broadcaster has long been candid about how parenthood shaped her career ambitions.

“I knew from the time that I was pregnant that I was not going to be a stay-at-home mom,” she told Huffington Post in 2012. “I love working and I happen to believe that if you’re happy in your life and you’re happy in what you’re doing, it makes you a better person, it makes you a better mother, it makes you a better partner and it makes you better at your job.”

Scroll below a complete guide to King’s family:

William Bumpus, an attorney, was married to King from 1982 to 1993. They welcomed daughter Kirby in 1986, followed by son William Jr. in 1987. They ultimately divorced after the TV broadcaster discovered her spouse was having an affair with a friend.

“I’m not a huge fan of the woman I caught naked with my now ex-husband on June 24, 1990, at 9:16 p.m.,” King told Vanity Fair in July 2016. “But I don’t remember the details.”

The couple initially attempted to reconcile through counseling before divorcing in 1993. Speaking on the “Call Her Daddy” podcast in May 2026, King said she realized Bumpus “hadn’t really changed” and that she “didn’t like” who she was becoming during that time.

“I would be out in the garage feeling the hood of the car to see if it was warm. I was going through his phone. And I thought, ‘I don’t want to live like this,’ only to find out he was cheating again,” she said.

Bumpus publicly apologized to King in 2016, calling himself “haunted” by his choice, and again after the “Call Her Daddy” episode aired.

“My deepest apologies to Gayle, to our daughter Kirby and her husband, Virgil, to our son William and his wife, Elise, and to our three grandchildren, for the pain I caused decades ago,” he said. “Those actions were mine.”

Kirby, King’s firstborn, arrived in 1986. She married Virgil Miller in 2020. Miller died in November 2026 after a private battle with cancer.

Further details about Miller’s diagnosis were not immediately publicly shared.

In addition to Kirby, Miller is survived by their two children: son Luca, born in 2021, and daughter Grayson, born in 2024. Luca, for his part, holds a special place in his grandmother’s world.

Before her April 2025 Blue Origin flight, she turned to Luca for emotional support — in stuffed-animal form.

“I just asked my favorite grandson, ‘Could you pick out your favorite animal, one of your favorite stuffed animals, that could go with me to space and keep ‘Gyla’ company?'” King exclusively told Us in April 2025. “So he’s looking.”

William Jr., born in 1987, is King’s second child and only son. He is married wife Elise Smith, with whom he shares one child.

While William Jr. has largely stayed out of the spotlight, King has often spoken about how important it was to her that both of her children grow up with a strong relationship with their father, even after the divorce.

“Once it is an issue, you have to balance what’s most important to you,” she said on “The Pivot” podcast in 2024. “I don’t care how successful you are, if your kids aren’t happy and healthy and adjusted. All this success means nothing.”

Daniella Karagach has secured a plum job for her 3-year-old daughter, Nikita, when her Dancing With the Stars partner Ezra Frech ties the knot someday.

“My daughter is going to be the flower girl at his wedding,” Karagach, 33, announced during a Wednesday, November 25, appearance on Hulu’s “Get Real” podcast, before joking, “She’ll be like 12 when he gets married.”

The Paralympian, 21, is currently single but he confirmed that Karagach has indeed locked up a ceremonial role for little Nikita whenever he does walk down the aisle. (Karagach and her husband, fellow DWTS pro Pasha Pashkov, welcomed their daughter in May 2023.)

Fresh off their mirrorball trophy win on Tuesday, November 24, “Get Real” host Amanda Hirsch expressed hope that Karagach and Frech will remain close now that season 35 is over.

“One thousand percent [we will],” Frech assured. “We’re going to be friends or family for life. We’ll dance together again.”

Karagach got emotional as she discussed the possibility of pairing up with another celebrity in 2027 given her immense success with Frech. (The DWTS pro previously won the mirrorball trophy in 2021 with celebrity partner Iman Shumpert.)

“How am I going to move on from him as a partner? What am I going to do?” Karagach wondered during the podcast interview.

The pair made history in Tuesday’s DWTS season 35 finale when their three dances received a combined score of 90 out of 90 from judges Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough, landing them in a three-way tie with Amber Glenn and Pashkov as well as Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas. Viewers’ votes ultimately delivered Frech and Karagach the mirrorball when factored into the final scores.

Earlier that night, Frech and Karagach triumphed with their freestyle even though the Paralympian struggled to get his prosthetic onto his leg.

“Last night was crazy. … I can’t believe this happened,” Frech recalled on Good Morning America on Wednesday morning. “I can’t believe we got that opportunity to represent [the disabled community].”

Frech shared how his professional partner proved to be crucial in helping him regain his focus following the mishap.

“We started our freestyle without the prosthetic; that was a creative choice, and then things went a little off script,” the athlete explained. “I wasn’t able to suction my leg on and I knew it wasn’t on. Sometimes when that happens, it’ll re-suction, but it didn’t. It came off. She told me to put it on mid-dance, I kinda blacked out.”

He added, “When it came off, I was like, ‘I’m doing the rest of the dance without my leg on.’ And I heard [Daniella] go, ‘Put your leg on!’”

“I saw his face, I was like, ‘If I don’t tell him to put his leg on, he’s gonna do the whole dance without it,” Karagach concurred.

Dancing With the Stars is expected to return to ABC and Disney+ in 2027.
